evidence.quote: This study follows a quantitative and explanatory research design to assess the influence of developer onboarding practices on the scalability of business applications within the Sri Lankan IT companies.
104 responses were gathered through a five-point Likert scale questionnaire, which was analyzed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS software
The bootstrapping process was used to assess the significance of path coefficients with 5,000 resamples.
The snowball sampling technique was adapted to reach specialized groups.
Through a quantitative approach, this research aims at medium and large-scale IT organizations of Sri Lanka, employing a non-random sampling technique.

Results indicate that the utilization of AI-assisted tools during the onboarding process allows developers to better adapt to the development environment by automating any repetitive tasks and enhancing their coding efficiency
In addition to this, a self-reported questionnaire was implemented for our data collection, which increases the possibility of a common method bias.
